statement: Neanderthal genetic ancestry in living human populations varies by population and is not one global figure: approximately 1.8-2.1% in Europeans and approximately 2.3-2.6% in East Asians (East Asians carrying roughly 12-20% more than Europeans, an asymmetry whose cause is disputed), with West African populations carrying a smaller (~0.3%) signal now attributed to back-migration of Eurasian, Neanderthal-ancestry-carrying lineages into Africa within roughly the last 20,000-50,000 years, rather than a separate direct African-Neanderthal admixture event.
scholarly_disagreement: The cause of the higher Neanderthal-ancestry fraction in East Asians than Europeans is disputed: differential efficiency of purifying selection (Sankararaman et al. 2014) versus an additional pulse of Neanderthal gene flow specifically into East Asian ancestors, which selection/drift alone cannot fully explain (Vernot & Akey 2015).

interpretations.position: Differential efficiency of purifying selection against deleterious Neanderthal variants explains the Europe/East-Asia asymmetry
Selection and reduced population size alone cannot explain the asymmetry; an additional gene-flow pulse into East Asian ancestors is required

does_not_demonstrate: that sub-Saharan African populations carry zero Neanderthal ancestry — that older framing is now an outdated oversimplification per Chen et al. 2020
